hook: Locker gold went 'missing', but an undated photo wasn't *proof*
hook_b: Locker gold went 'missing', but an undated photo wasn't *proof*
tldr: The Telangana State Consumer Commission upheld a district order dismissing a claim that gold coins, bars and melted gold went missing from a jointly held SBI locker in Hyderabad.

beats.what: The holders said they kept about 200 g of gold in 2015; in 2016 eight coins, two bars and some melted gold were found missing.
beats.why: The bank said a locker needs two keys, only holders know its contents, and there was no sign of the locker being forced.
beats.care: Banks don't record what's inside a locker, so your own dated proof of contents is what counts if anything goes missing.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI (Nov 17): police had classified the theft case as 'undetectable'; the commission let the holders pursue their pending protest petition.

cards.q: Should banks share responsibility for what goes missing from lockers?
opts: Only if the locker was forced

qs: What proof should locker holders keep of what's inside?
Who bears the risk when a locker isn't forced but items go missing?

facts.t: Opening the locker needs *two keys*, one with the customer and one with the bank.
Holders said *eight* gold coins, two bars and melted gold were missing.

viz.verdict: Holders lost at both consumer forums; police case still open

steps.e: Gold kept in locker, per holders

watch: The pending protest petition against the police's 'undetectable' closure of the theft case.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Woman, granddaughter allege gold missing from locker; but commission rejects claim

fact: Consumer commission rejected a *200-gram* locker gold loss claim against SBI Gunfoundry
twist: The deciding factor: their only proof was a photo with no date or signature.
